title: Treat `Config/Needs/website` like `Imports`?
description:
I ran `use_tidy_description()` on a package with:

```
Config/Needs/website:
    tidyverse/tidytemplate
```

and it converted it to:

```
Config/Needs/website:tidyverse/tidytemplate
```

Notice that it also removed the space, which seems wrong. At the very least I think it should keep that.

I managed to reproduce this with dev desc. The other weird thing is that if you run `use_tidy_description()` again on the "tidied" file, then it adds the space back.

``` r
tf <- tempfile()

# With Config/Needs/website
text <- "Config/Needs/website:\n\ttidyverse/tidytemplate"
desc <- desc::description$new(text = text)
desc$normalize()
desc$write(file = tf)
readLines(tf)
#> [1] "Config/Needs/website:tidyverse/tidytemplate"


# With Imports
text <- "Imports:\n\trlang"
desc <- desc::description$new(text = text)
desc$normalize()
desc$write(file = tf)
readLines(tf)
#> [1] "Imports:"  "    rlang"


# Notice how it actually adds the space back if you run it again?
text <- "Config/Needs/website:tidyverse/tidytemplate"
desc <- desc::description$new(text = text)
desc$normalize()
desc$write(file = tf)
readLines(tf)
#> [1] "Config/Needs/website: tidyverse/tidytemplate"
```

title: Error in read.dcf(con) : Line starting 'desc/ ...' is malformed!
description:
When a package file does not follow the standard `pkg_ver.tar.gz` filename, desc assumes it to be a plain text file, resulting in a weird error:


```r
download.file("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/desc/desc_1.4.2.tar.gz", "desc.tar.gz")
desc::description$new("desc.tar.gz")
# Error in read.dcf(con) : Line starting 'desc/ ...' is malformed!
# In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
```

This happens because:

https://github.com/r-lib/desc/blob/6e32ba71072a1e17a9e643ad5e15d30948c31015/R/package-archives.R#L1-L4

Perhaps we should error if the file is a zip/gz but does not pass `is_valid_package_file_name(file)`. Or we could make it more flexible to try and extract `*/DESCRIPTION` without knowing the package name in advance.

title: Add `desc_url_git()`?
description:
@gaborcsardi Would you be open to accept a PR introducing a function `desc_url_git()` à la:

```r
#' Get Git repository URL from `DESCRIPTION` file
#'
#' Returns the first Git repository URL found in the `URL` (preferred) or `BugReports` fields of a `DESCRIPTION` file.
#'
#' Currently, this function recognizes [GitLab](https://about.gitlab.com/), [GitHub](https://github.com/), [Gitea](https://gitea.com/),
#' [Codeberg](https://codeberg.org/), [Pagure](https://pagure.io/), [Bitbucket](https://bitbucket.org/) and [SourceHut](https://sr.ht/) repository URLs.
#'
#' @inheritParams desc::desc_get_field
#'
#' @return A character scalar.
#' @export
desc_url_git <- function(file = ".") {
  
  desc::desc_get_field(key = "BugReports",
                       default = character(),
                       file = file) |>
    stringr::str_replace(pattern = "/issues/?$",
                         replacement = "/") %>%
    c(desc::desc_get_urls(), .) |>
    stringr::str_subset(pattern = "^https?://(git(hub|lab|ea)\\..+|(codeberg|bitbucket)\\.org|(git\\.)?src\\.ht|pagure\\.io)/") |>
    dplyr::first()
}
```

Of course, I'd rewrite it in base R to avoid introducing additional package dependencies (stringr, magrittr).

title: Better formatting with `$set_list()`
description:
I'm using the new `$get_list()` and `$set_list()` to (conditionally) add "tidyverse/tidytemplate" to the "Config/Needs/website" field from usethis (https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/1408). I am very excited to find the new get/set support for list-y fields.

But I predict it won't be long before I get a complaint about the resulting formatting of this field, so I'm getting a head start by just opening this issue now 😅

I wish it were easier to to get formatting in the style of, say, Imports or Remotes.

Here's an example of what I'm seeing:

Before:

```
Config/Needs/website:
    tidyverse,
    r-lib/downlit
```

After:

```
Config/Needs/website:tidyverse, r-lib/downlit, tidyverse/tidytemplate
```

There is no longer a line break or any whitespace after the `:` and we've switched from one package per line to comma delimited.

If I request `sep = "\n"`, after looks like this (I'm including more context):

```

Suggests: 
    covr,
    curl,
    downlit,
    dplyr (>= 1.0.0),
    knitr,
    mockr,
    rmarkdown,
    roxygen2,
    sodium,
    spelling,
    testthat (>= 3.0.0)
VignetteBuilder: 
    knitr
Config/Needs/website:tidyverse
 r-lib/downlit
 tidyverse/tidytemplate
```

There's still no whitespace after the `:` and the subsequent lines aren't indented to the same depth as other list-y fields.

Here is the heart of the helper that's doing this:

``` r
an_internal_helper <- function(...) {
  desc <- desc::desc(file = proj_get())
...
  if (append) {
    values <- unique(c(desc$get_list(key, default = ""), values))
  }
  desc$set_list(key, values)
  #desc$set_list(key, values, sep = "\n")
...
  desc$write()
}
```

If the field is entirely absent to begin with, the result looks OK (i.e. we do get a space after `:`):

```
Config/Needs/website: tidyverse/tidytemplate
```

description:
When reading description files with ‘Author’ and ‘Maintainer’ fields (but without ‘<Authors\@R>’) and with roles specified in brackets, the maintainer/author is not returned as an author by `get_author(s)()`.

Example from [WRE](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#The-DESCRIPTION-file) (again without ‘<Authors\@R>’):

``` r
library(desc)

d <- desc(text =
            "Package: pkgname

Date: 2015-01-01
Title: My First Collection of Functions
Author: Joe Developer [aut, cre],
  Pat Developer [aut],
  A. User [ctb]
Maintainer: Joe Developer <Joe.Developer@some.domain.net>
Depends: R (>= 3.1.0), nlme
Suggests: MASS
Description: A (one paragraph) description of what
  the package does and why it may be useful.
License: GPL (>= 2)
URL: https://www.r-project.org, http://www.another.url
BugReports: https://pkgname.bugtracker.url"
)

d$coerce_authors_at_r()
```

title: Encoding error on R 4.2 (devel)
description:
Hi,

I'm encountering an error that I'm not 100% sure that is due to `desc`. It might be given the traceback information, hence why I'm reporting it here. But if belongs elsewhere, please let me know.

I'd appreciate you taking a look at this.

Thanks in advance!
Leo

## Error description

My GitHub Actions workflow for my `biocthis` package using the GitHub version of `pkgdown` errored out with 

```R
Error in iconv(mat[], from = "UTF-8", to = encoding) : 
  unsupported conversion from 'UTF-8' to 'Encoding: UTF-8'
```

at https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4292895831?check_suite_focus=true#step:28:94. The traceback information https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4292895831?check_suite_focus=true#step:28:88 shows that `base:::iconv(mat[], from = "UTF-8", to = encoding)` is involved after `desc$write(file = tf)`. `Encoding: UTF-8` likely comes from the `biocthis` DESCRIPTION at https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/blob/0bbf986a2713a89012e5f85ce90b9f3101435ff6/DESCRIPTION#L16. 

## Locating the error source

The error is originated by https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/blob/master/vignettes/biocthis.Rmd#L128 which uses several `usethis` functions https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/blob/master/R/biocthis_example_pkg.R, in particular `usethis::create_package()` which uses `desc$write` at https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/main/R/description.R#L71. `desc` in turn uses `base::iconv()` at https://github.com/r-lib/desc/blob/daece0e5816e17a461969489bfdda2d50b4f5fe5/R/description.R#L796.

## GHA runs

My GHA with R 4.2 (current devel) was using `desc` 1.4.0 https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4292895831?check_suite_focus=true#step:21:71. The same code but with R 4.1 and the CRAN version of `pkgdown` did work https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4293462431?check_suite_focus=true#step:21:70. 

| |  run 1 | run 2 |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| R session info | [GHA](https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4292895831?check_suite_focus=true#step:21:71) | [GHA](https://github.com/lcolladotor/biocthis/runs/4293462431?check_suite_focus=true#step:21:70) |
| status | fails | runs |
| R | 4.2 (devel) | 4.1 |
| pkgdown | 1.9000.9000.9000 r-lib/pkgdown@e72fc30 | 1.6.1 |
| usethis | 2.1.3 | 2.1.3 |
| desc | 1.4.0 | 1.4.0 |

## Is it a `desc` issue with R 4.2 (devel)? 

Rather than this being a `pkgdown` issue, I'm guessing that maybe `desc` provides information that `base::iconv()` doesn't like anymore in R devel. But I'm not sure. I see that 20 days ago `desc` did pass all checks with R devel https://github.com/r-lib/desc/runs/4083193323?check_suite_focus=true. That would be after https://github.com/r-lib/desc/pull/112/commits/67d28126b13f44400134e9aa22e3ba9dde1ad4d0 which well, changed how `desc$write` works in relation to encoding.

Maybe this is not relevant since both GHA runs used `usethis` version 2.1.3. I see that `usethis` changed 2 months ago and started using `desc$write` from https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blame/main/R/description.R#L71 at https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/commit/8b11a5f2ba49f03b5d43f099170475fa0caa68fc. Though also 21 days ago I see that it passed its tests on R devel https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/runs/4073956879?check_suite_focus=true.

title: Change formatting of Authors@R under normalization
description:
I've been able to remove lots of code from usethis by delegating various DESCRIPTION operations to desc, which is great.

However one consequence is that we're getting some undesirable re-styling of the Authors@R field (via, e.g. `usethis::use_tidy_description()`.

GOOD, YES:

```
Authors@R: c(
    person("Hadley", "Wickham", , "hadley@rstudio.com", role = c("aut", "cre"), 
      comment = c(ORCID = "0000-0003-4757-117X")
    ),
    person("Jennifer", "Bryan", , "jenny@rstudio.com", role = "aut",
      comment = c(ORCID = "0000-0002-6983-2759")
    ),
    person("RStudio", role = c("cph", "fnd"))
  )
```

BAD, NO:

```
Authors@R: 
    c(person(given = "Hadley",
             family = "Wickham",
             role = c("aut", "cre"),
             email = "hadley@rstudio.com"),
      person(given = "Robby",
             family = "Shaver",
             role = "aut"),
      person(given = "RStudio",
             role = "cph"))
```

If it's OK, it's much nicer to implement this behaviour here and inherit it in usethis. Sound OK?

`usethis::use_tidy_description()` calls `desc$normalize()`, so the thing to change is somewhere inside there.

title: Reading DESCRIPTION fails when empty lines present
description:
(Discovered investigating https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/1436)

When a `DESCRIPTION` file has an extra space it in, desc trips up and doesn't provide a helpful error message

``` r
desc <- 'Package: desc.empty.line
Title: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
Version: 0.0.0.9000
Authors@R: 
    person(given = "First",
           family = "Last",
           role = c("aut", "cre"),
           email = "first.last@example.com",
           comment = c(ORCID = "YOUR-ORCID-ID"))
Description: What the package does (one paragraph).

License: `use_mit_license()`, `use_gpl3_license()` or friends to pick a
    license
Encoding: UTF-8
Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)
RoxygenNote: 7.1.1
'

desc::desc(text = desc)
#> Error in if (any(mismatch <- res != res2)) {: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

<sup>Created on 2021-04-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

The problem seems to be here: https://github.com/r-lib/desc/blob/1a9af2d57b92de577e4cd67f126a4f1461554db6/R/read.R#L18-L29

Essentially, when `read.dcf()` encounters a new line, it treats it as a whole new record and adds a row to the output with whatever is left in the DCF file. 

It seems reasonable for `DESCRIPTION` files to check this in `read_desc()`, e.g.

```r
if (nrow(res)) > 1) {
  stop("Empty lines found in DESCRIPTION file", call. = FALSE)
}
```

Happy to submit a PR if you think that will do the trick, as well as to add a test

title: desc::desc() output inconsistent with read.dcf()
description:
While somewhat related to #14, this issue is actually about leading white space, not trailing space.

Given this DESCRIPTION
```
Package: test
Title: What the Package Does (one line, title case)
Version: 0.0.0.9000
Authors@R: person("First", "Last", email = "first.last@example.com", role = c("aut", "cre"))
Description: What the package does (one paragraph).
Depends: R (>= 3.5.1)
License: What license is it under?
Encoding: UTF-8
LazyData: true
RoxygenNote: 6.1.0.9000
Collate:
    'b-function.R'
    'a-function.R'
Imports: magrittr,
    readr
```
With `read.dcf()`, you get the following
```
> dcf <- read.dcf("DESCRIPTION")
> dcf[,which(colnames(dcf) == "Collate")]
                         Collate 
"'b-function.R'\n'a-function.R'" 
> dcf[,which(colnames(dcf) == "Imports")]
           Imports 
"magrittr,\nreadr" 
```

However, with `desc::desc()` you get
```
> dcf <- desc::desc("DESCRIPTION")
> dcf$get_field("Collate")
[1] "'b-function.R'\n    'a-function.R'"
> dcf$get_field("Imports")
[1] "magrittr,\n    readr"
```

The additional white space between values causes `roxygen2::parse_package()` to fail when processing a package that uses collation as it results in a list with blank entries that get translated to directory names instead of file names.

While you can make the case that `roxygen2` should be more rigorous in it's checking (klutometis/roxygen#766), you should at least document that the pattern above is not a drop-in replacement for `base::read.dcf()`

title: Ideas for validate?
description:
Messy list of ideas 😸 I'm not sure what's validate vs what's "best-practice"cf https://github.com/r-lib/desc/issues/74#issuecomment-426989817

* valid URLs (`crul::ok()` or `httr` equivalent) anywhere where there's an URL - including checking whether there's a redirect, i.e. when a repo was transferred to a new owner on GitHub, the URL should be changed although the old one is still valid because redirected.
* has the URLs (BugReports, Repository)
* only roles that exist
* no duplicate authors (tricky one when not for exact match)
* the description check that's already done somewhere else (stating it shouldn't start by "This package")
* no duplicate dependency, e.g. the same package twice once under Depends once under Suggests
* no missing necessary field
* no non-accepted field
* ORCIDs (_that_ would be "best-practice" and quite opiniated so probably not in scope)
* Anything that's in `R CMD Check` reg DESCRIPTION except with regard to the rest of the package.

title: Trailing whitespace behavior when moving dependencies to multiple lines
description:
**desc** tries very hard to preserve trailing whitespace, however there is one place maybe we should be removing it.

If you have a dependency on the first line, and desc reformats the fields so they are on multiple lines, the trailing whitespace on the first line is preserved.

```
Depends: pkg1, pkg2, pkg3
```
```
Depends: <- space here
  pkg1,
  pkg2
  pkg3
```

While the current behavior is technically correct (there was a space after the `:`) I think it is generally not what is desired in this case. Either the behavior could be tweaked when splitting dependencies across lines or perhaps a function to strip all trailing whitespace could be added?

First observed at https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/49
